finding.shodan.vulnerabilities: Shodan associates {count} CVE(s) with this address (most severe: {cve}); inferred from announced versions, to be verified
module.shodan.checks: Queries Shodan for the target IP address: indexed ports and services, products and versions, host names and CVEs. Without a key, the free InternetDB database is used.
module.shodan.fix:
Compare what Shodan sees (ports, products, versions, host names) with what you actually run: any unexpected port or service is an exposure to close right away in the firewall (see the "Open ports" module).
If Shodan shows a data or administration service reachable without protection (database, Docker, VNC, RDP), close it first, then treat it as compromised: change its passwords and keys, read its logs.
For each CVE, check that it really applies to you. Shodan infers it from the announced version, yet distributions (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat) often fix flaws without changing the version number: look for the CVE in the package changelog (snippets below) or in the distribution's security advisory.
If the CVE applies, install the security update (`apt update && apt upgrade` or `dnf upgrade`) and restart the service concerned, or failing that apply the vendor's workaround (disable the feature, filter access). Handle the most serious CVEs first, and those in the CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities (KEV).
If the address belongs to a CDN, a load balancer or shared hosting, these ports and CVEs describe the provider and not your server: examine the server's origin address (the "Origin IP behind a CDN" module).
Give Shodan time to come back with its probes before concluding the fix worked: the record does not update immediately (the free InternetDB database is refreshed every week).
Monitor over time: create a Shodan alert on your addresses to be warned when a new port or service appears, and rerun this module after every infrastructure change.
See without a key what Shodan knows about your address with the `curl` command in the snippet below (ports, host names, CVEs and tags as JSON).
module.shodan.fix_snippet:
# InternetDB
curl -s https://internetdb.shodan.io/203.0.113.10

# Debian / Ubuntu
apt changelog openssh-server | grep CVE-YYYY-NNNN

# RHEL / Fedora
rpm -q --changelog openssh-server | grep CVE-YYYY-NNNN
module.shodan.title: Shodan
module.shodan.why: Shodan shows the target the way Internet scanners see it: a forgotten service, an exposed database or a vulnerable version often appears there before it is fixed.
shodan.not_public: Non-public address: Shodan not applicable (no third-party service queried)
shodan.score_vulns: {count} CVE(s) reported by Shodan (to be verified)
